newsitem.title: USA: Ag biotech key to feeding world, US Sen Lugar says.
newsitem.headline: Ag biotech key to feeding world, US Sen Lugar says.

text.p: Genetically engineered crops will be vital in feeding the world's growing population, the chairman of the Senate Agriculture Committee said Monday in urging the United States to lead the field.
"Today, the United States is the global leader in agricultural biotechnology," chairman Richard Lugar, Indiana Republican, said in a speech to U.S. agricultural attaches.
"We must continue this role, discouraging other countries -- such as those in the European Union -- from stifling biotechnology.
"If we do not make tremendous strides in biotechnology, we will experience a head-on collision. This is one we cannot afford to lose and the European Union cannot afford to win."

During his remarks, Lugar cited estimates that yields must triple by 2050 to feed the expected global population of nine billion at that time. He said there was consensus that biotech crops "must florish if growing world food demand is to be met."

U.S. and EU officials have clashed strongly over EU rules that call for labeling of foods made with biotech crops and demands by some EU activists that biotech crops be handled, stored and sold separately from other crops. U.S. officials say labeling is unneeded in most cases and that separate sales systems would be unduly costly.
